contracts.boundary: The reviewed production index.ts sha256 is declared once in tests/fixtures/replay-fault-control.mjs and the six integration fault gates import that constant, so rebinding the reviewed baseline is a one-file change and no gate can drift to a different reviewed hash.
contracts.assertions: Each gate's baseline equals the imported REPLAY_GUARD_BASELINE_SHA256; gate proofs still start GREEN on the pristine reviewed source, turn the named assertion RED under the controlled production mutation, restore the source, and record restored GREEN; Rebasing the baseline touches exactly one file and all six gates observe the same value.

contracts.boundary: One local command rebinds the per-change declaration to a reviewed base and validates the shape the acceptance run enforces: the base resolves to a real commit, is an ancestor of HEAD, matches the declaration's base field, and declared files exactly cover diff(base, HEAD). The helper never connects to the network and never edits anything but the declaration file.
contracts.assertions: resolveBaseRef uses --verify so a ref that names no commit in the object database fails; a base outside HEAD's ancestry fails with a named detail; --apply rewrites only the declaration base in place and is idempotent; coverage reports file set differences in both directions without guessing; the CLI exits 0 with a report only when the declaration matches the requested base and its file list exactly covers the candidate diff, exits 1 with a report naming each uncovered file, exits 1 without a report when the base cannot resolve, and prints usage on malformed operands; validation without --apply never writes.

boundaryTest.name: exits 0 with the passed report and exits 1 on a stale diff report

invariant.name: validates against the requested base and --apply rebases only the declaration base

fault.exception: The helper is a deterministic structure check over its own inputs with no production behavior to mutate; assertion sensitivity is established by executed mutation checks against the helper in this change (dropping changedNotDeclared turns 2 cases RED and ignoring declarationMatches turns 1 case RED) and the CLI fault case above.
